extracted.intended_audience: Principal investigators (PIs), authorized organizational officials (AORs)/Sponsored Projects Offices, NSF Program Officers, external reviewers and panelists involved in NSF proposal submission, review, and post-review processes.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on NSF proposal submission, merit review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts), reviewer selection, allowed proposal updates, negotiation/revision rules during review, funding recommendation and award decision processes, and appeal and disclosure procedures. Intended to govern how proposals are evaluated and processed across NSF programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principle: highest quality and potential to advance knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF projects should be of the highest quality and have the potential to advance, if not transform, the frontiers of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle should be given due diligence by PIs/organizations when preparing proposals, by reviewers when evaluating, and by NSF staff when recommending funding and overseeing awards. It forms the basis for assessing Intellectual Merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principle: contribution to societal goals (Broader Impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF projects, in aggregate, should contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals. Broader impacts may be accomplished through the research itself, activities directly related to the project, or activities supported by but complementary to the project. Activities may be based on established or innovative methods but must be well justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs should clearly state goals and describe activities; reviewers assess how projects advance NSF’s mission and societal outcomes. Broader impacts need justification and may be implemented at project or aggregated levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principle: meaningful assessment and appropriate metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful assessment and evaluation of NSF-funded projects should be based on appropriate metrics, considering likely correlation between broader impacts and resources provided. Small activities’ outcomes may be best assessed at a higher, aggregated level than the individual project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs are expected to be accountable: include clearly stated goals, specific activity descriptions, and a plan to document outputs. Reviewers should consider whether assessment plans are appropriate given scope and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate what the proposers want to do, why, how, how they will know if they succeed, and the potential benefits if successful, with attention to novelty, rigor, and potential to advance understanding within or across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criterion: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration includes benefits to society, educational impacts, broadening participation, and other positive outcomes. Address both project-level activities and potential aggregated contributions; include justification and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in reviews: advance knowledge / societal benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to advance knowledge and understanding within its field or across fields (Intellectual Merit) and to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes (Broader Impacts)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly weigh both advancement of knowledge and societal benefits when forming assessments; both criteria receive full consideration and neither alone is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in reviews: creativity and potential to transform
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess novelty and transformative potential as part of Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts where applicable; innovative approaches should be identified and evaluated for plausibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in reviews: quality of plan and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include clarity of objectives, methodology, timelines, milestones, and explicit evaluation/assessment plans appropriate to project scale and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in reviews: qualifications of individuals/teams
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should consider expertise, track record, complementary skills, and whether personnel are appropriate to project scope and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements to consider in reviews: adequacy of resources and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate institutional facilities, collaborations, budget realism, and whether requested resources match project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of reviewers: special knowledge of subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimal reviewers should have special knowledge of the science and engineering subfields involved in the proposals to evaluate competence, intellectual merit, and utility of the proposed activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within reasonable limits, reviewer specialties should be complementary within a reviewer group to cover technical aspects thoroughly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of reviewers: broader/generalized knowledge for Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have broader or more generalized knowledge of relevant subfields to evaluate broader impacts, especially for large/complex, interdisciplinary, or nationally/internationally significant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewers with broader expertise when proposals have substantial size, complexity, or cross-disciplinary content to assess potential societal contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of reviewers: knowledge of science & engineering infrastructure and educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should have broad knowledge of the infrastructure of the science and engineering enterprise and its educational activities to evaluate contributions to societal goals, personnel development, and distribution of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps assess whether projects contribute appropriately to workforce development, infrastructure needs, and equitable distribution of resources across organizations/geographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of reviewers: diverse representation in reviewer groups
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent possible, achieve diverse representation within the review group—consider organization type, reviewer diversity, age distribution, and geographic balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity is a stated goal to ensure balanced perspectives; Program Officers should seek reviewer groups with complementary backgrounds and demographic balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal file update: proposer organization responsibility and AOR authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the proposing organization to thoroughly review each proposal prior to submission. Requests to replace files or revise proposal attributes must be signed and submitted by the Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Submitted Proposals Module in Research.gov for updates; organizations’ SPOs can initiate or review requests. A Proposal Update Justification must be provided addressing why changes are requested and differences between original and replacement files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal file update: timing for automatic acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a proposal file update will automatically be accepted if submitted prior to: the deadline date; initiation of external peer review in cases when a target date is utilized; and initiation of external peer review in the case of an unsolicited proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted within these windows, replacement files immediately become part of the official proposal. Consult Research.gov guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal file update: restrictions after review initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a proposal file update after the specified timeframes requires acceptance by the cognizant NSF Program Officer and shall be submitted only to correct a technical problem (e.g., formatting or print problems). Changes in proposal content should not be requested after the timeframes specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, the replacement files immediately replace existing files and become official. Proposers should not use updates to circumvent content/deadline rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal file update: one request at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF will consider only one request for a proposal file update per proposal at a time. Multiple updates are expected to be rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan any necessary corrections carefully to avoid multiple sequential requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions during review: obligation to notify Program Officer of significant developments
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a significant development (e.g., research findings, changed circumstances, unavailability of PI or senior personnel) that might materially affect the outcome of the review of a pending proposal, the proposer must contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer to discuss the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting additional information must not be used to circumvent page limitations or deadlines. Program Officers may advise on appropriate action or whether a formal update is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions during review: limitations on negotiations and what may be discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Before recommending funding, Program Officers may engage in discussions with PIs; negotiating budgets generally involves discussing lower or higher total support and suggesting reduction/elimination of clearly unnecessary or unreasonable budget items. This generally does not include faculty salaries, salary rates, fringe benefits, or tuition. Indirect cost (F&A) rates are not subject to negotiation. Program Officers may not renegotiate cost sharing or other organizational commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget discussions focus on aligning scope with available funds; any substantial changes may require formal revised materials via Research.gov and appropriate signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions during review: required actions when budget cut ≥10%
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussions result in a budget reduction of 10% or more from the amount originally proposed, a corresponding reduction should be made in project scope. A revised proposal budget, budget justification, and a Budget Impact Statement describing the impact of the reduction on scope must be provided. Revised budgets must be signed and submitted by the AOR using the Submitted Proposals Module in Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Budget Impact Statement must clearly explain how scope, deliverables, and timelines change due to the budget reduction; AOR signature is required to validate organizational concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding recommendation: Program Officer role and award abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: After scientific, technical, and programmatic review and consideration, the NSF Program Officer recommends to the cognizant Division Director whether the proposal should be declined or recommended for award. If recommended, the PI may be contacted to assist in preparing the public award abstract and title which justify the expenditure of Federal funds by articulating how the project serves the national interest as stated by NSF's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Program Officer’s recommendation does not constitute an obligation of funds; only an appointed NSF Grants and Agreements Officer may make commitments or authorize expenditures. PIs should not make financial/personnel commitments before an award notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to award: DGA/DACS pre-award review and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If programmatic approval is obtained, the recommended proposal goes to the Division of Grants and Agreements (DGA) or the Division of Acquisition and Cooperative Support (DACS) for review of business, financial, and policy implications, including utilization of NSF’s risk-based framework to evaluate proposer risks prior to issuing an award. DGA generally makes the decision to award or decline within 30 days after the program Division/Office recommendation, though special cases may require more time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals with prior inactivity, coordination with other agencies, cooperative agreements, proposals >$20M, or unusual considerations may undergo extended review and processing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process for declines due to financial/administrative reasons: informal clarification and formal review
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposer declined for an NSF award for reasons related to pre-award financial and administrative reviews may discuss the decline with the cognizant NSF Grants and Agreements Officer or Branch Chief. If dissatisfied, the proposing organization’s AOR may submit a request for review to the Division Director of DGA or DACS within 30 days of the declination notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request need not follow a prescribed format but must contain a full statement of the proposer’s position, facts, reasons, and supporting documentation. New information not available at the time the decision was made will not be considered (e.g., new financial stability information). The review will be conducted by officials not involved in the original decision, with timelines: the reviewer(s) forward a report within 30 days of receipt, and the Division Director normally communicates the final decision within 15 days of receipt of that report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appeal process: applicability limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal process described applies only to declinations arising from pre-award financial and administrative reviews by DGA or DACS; it does not apply to proposals returned or declined for other reasons, nor are proposals declined for administrative/financial reasons eligible for reconsideration under other chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should confirm the reason for declination in the notice to determine whether this appeal route is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review information provided to PI upon decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision (award or declination) has been made, NSF releases electronically to the PI: a description of the review process used; copies of all reviews used in the decision (reviewer-identifying information redacted); panel summary and recommendation if reviewed by a panel; and site-visit reports if applicable. If not in the panel summary, PI is provided a written explanation of the basis for declination. PIs may request other releasable material from NSF’s file on the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material identifying reviewers or identifying other pending or declined proposals is usually withheld. Reviews are provided to help PIs improve research and proposals; they are not intended for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of recipient proposal information and FOIA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that result in an NSF award will be made available to the public on request consistent with the Freedom of Information Act, except for privileged, personal, proprietary, or otherwise legally exempt information. Appropriate labeling in the proposal aids identification of exempt material; such information will be withheld to the extent permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portions of awarded proposals describing inventions where the Government or recipient has rights will normally be withheld until a reasonable time has been allowed for filing patent applications. NSF will notify recipients of requests for copies so recipients may advise NSF of inventions or other confidential/commercial information.
